## Working directly on disk, no re-uploading files into a chat each time

**The problem:** the same small research tasks (convert a PDF, scaffold a
workflow, write up a report) get re-solved from scratch in every
conversation with a coding agent.

. . .

**This repo:** a set of `SKILL.md`-based skills a coding agent reads and
runs itself — the agent does the work, the skill just teaches it how.

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
The repo's name reflects where this started — a local-library toolkit —
not its current, broader scope.
:::

## Five skills, domain-agnostic

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
- **`pdf-to-markdown`** — convert a PDF to searchable markdown via a
  local GPU/CPU OCR pipeline, no API key, no internet after first run
- **`local-library`** — organize a folder of documents into an indexed,
  summarized, agent-navigable library
- **`workflow`** — scaffold and extend reproducible Snakemake pipelines
- **`reporting`** — author and render one-off Quarto reports, logs, and
  (as of this deck) presentations
- **`agent-runner`** — launch a coding agent session from a script, so an
  agent can be one step in an otherwise scriptable pipeline
:::

## Two different kinds of problem, two different fixes {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Scripted** (deterministic)

- scaffolding a new document/workflow/library
- finding existing ones
- cleaning up render output

Small helper scripts, covered by `python_unit_tests/`.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Judgment** (not scriptable)

- what story a report should tell
- how to classify and summarize a document
- when a workflow needs its own rule vs. reusing one

Instructions in `SKILL.md`, validated by actually running the thing.
:::
::::

## One skill, every coding agent

```{python}
#| echo: true
import os
sorted(os.listdir("../skills"))
```

`scripts/activate-skills.py` symlinks every skill above into each known
agent's own project-scoped skill directory — `.claude/skills/`,
`.agents/skills/` (Antigravity, and Copilot CLI's alternate path),
`.codex/skills/`, `.vibe/skills/` — so editing a skill here shows up
immediately, for whichever agent you're actually running.

## Takeaways

<!-- speaker note for whoever presents this: pick 2-3, don't read all 3 verbatim -->

- **Domain-agnostic on purpose** — none of these five skills assume a
  particular research field, only a particular *kind* of task
- **Multi-agent by design, not by accident** — one `skills/` directory,
  wired into Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Antigravity, Codex CLI, and
  Mistral Vibe without duplicating a single file
- **Tested two ways** — fast, free `python_unit_tests/` for the scripts;
  slower, real-cost `skill_tests/` for whether the skills actually do
  their job end-to-end
